priorities.description: WRITE THE 1979 REBUILDING OF THE TRIPPING ETHIC INTO canoe-trips.md AND environmental-history.md AS A SEQUENCE. Three separate statements of leave-no-trace ethics appear in Canadian Camping within seven months: Kevin Redmond's 'No Trace Camping' (March 1979), with its group-size rule -- 'The organization of trips with more than 20 people is bound to leave its mark on the ecology' -- and its fire and latrine specifics; the twenty Environmental Maintenance Standards from a Conference of Canadian Interpreters (June 1979), which open on exactly Kanawana's own 1970 erosion problem and which question permanent out-trip sites, motor boats and even flush toilets; and 'Canoe Tripping in the Twentieth Century' (October 1979), which abandons four techniques standard in camping manuals -- trenches, bough beds, tables and garbage pits. Taken with the November 1975 flotation regulation and the association's reckoning after the 1978 Quebec fatality, the whole safety-and-ethics framework around a Quebec camp's wilderness tripping was rebuilt between 1975 and 1979, and none of it originated at Kanawana. The articles should say so and date it, so that later Kanawana environmental commitments are read as joining a movement rather than leading one. | DONE 2026-09-05, and HALF OF IT WAS ALREADY DONE. environmental-history.md already carried Redmond's March 1979 'No Trace Camping' and the June 1979 Environmental Maintenance Standards, read against Kanawana's own 1970 erosion confession. What was missing was canoe-trips.md, where the gap was exactly at 1979 -- its chronology ran '1978: a fatal wilderness trip in Quebec' straight into 'What the movement decided, 1980'. A section '1979: the tripping ethic itself is rebuilt' now sits between them, carrying all three statements with their specifics: Redmond's warning to 'beware of the traditions -- axes, saws, elaborate latrines, garbage pits and material shelters, all of which can be found in camping texts' and his test ('Will the next traveller, be he a couple of hours or years away, know that you have been there?'); the twenty standards, cross-linked to the environmental article rather than repeated; and the October 1979 canoe-tripping rules, ending on the four abandoned techniques -- trenches, bough beds, tables and garbage pits. THE POINT THE PRIORITY ASKED FOR IS STATED IN THE ARTICLE: those four were not lapses but TECHNIQUE, printed in the manuals and taught to counsellors, and within seven months the national magazine told camps to stop all of them. And the framing the priority wanted: Kanawana's later environmental commitments read differently depending on whether the movement got there first, and it did -- the whole safety-and-ethics framework around a Quebec camp's wilderness tripping was rebuilt between 1975 and 1979 by people at other camps. The article says Kanawana joined a movement rather than led one, and adds the honest qualifier that no source shows it dissenting either. canoe-trips.md 22 -> 23 sources.
priorities.source: word-for-word read of Canadian Camping, issues 123-127, converted to KB facts

priorities.description: IDENTIFY THE FORMER LAURENTIAN BOYS' CAMP ADVERTISED FOR RENT IN OCTOBER 1979. The classified reads: 'Property for rent -- to clubs, community, religious, company or other groups for adult, children, or family camping; 75 acres, 3 lakes, large wharf, diving board and tower, playing field, buildings, electricity, central water system, FORMER BOYS' CAMP; weekly, monthly or season: 70 miles from Montreal near Lachute, Quebec.' Only a Montreal telephone number is given. A 75-acre three-lake site with a diving tower near Lachute is specific enough to identify from municipal assessment rolls, the Argenteuil regional county records, or the Quebec association's own membership directories for the 1960s and 1970s -- a camp that had closed by 1979 but was still standing. Match against connections/related-camps/quebec-camp-landscape.md, which is the register of camps Kanawana sat among; a closure in the 1970s is also a datum for the shrinking market Granek documented (p_321).
priorities.source: word-for-word read of Canadian Camping, issues 123-127, converted to KB facts

priorities.description: FIND THE QUEBEC ASSOCIATION'S OWN NEWSLETTER. Marjorie Booth, as the CCA's first Executive Director, wrote in February 1980: 'Many times I've come across great articles in provincial newsletters. If each province can continue (or begin?) to include C.C.A. on their mailing list for a few copies of newsletters, conference programs, etc., "Canadian Camping" will be able to carry articles from all parts of the country.' Much of what the national run prints from 1980 onward is reprinted from provincial newsletters -- which means the PROVINCIAL newsletters are a parallel body of material this project has never touched, and the Quebec one is the one to want. It would carry exactly what the national newsletter thins out: Quebec camp news, Quebec officer changes, Quebec conference programmes, and quite possibly Kanawana by name. The read has already shown the Quebec association producing substantial documents of its own -- the 1976 Director Education Program, the standards manual and its marking scheme, the Semaine des camps campaigns. Search: the ACQ's successor body; Trent, which received provincial as well as national camping papers; BAnQ; and the Quebec ministry fonds that funded the association's training programmes.
priorities.source: word-for-word read of Canadian Camping, issues 128-132, converted to KB facts

priorities.description: SPAWN A STUB FOR MARJORIE A. BOOTH -- and use it to fix a hole in camp-oolahwan.md. She was the Canadian Camping Association's first Executive Director, appointed in November 1979 on a Fitness and Amateur Sport grant, and came to it directly from being 'the director of Camp Oolahwan, the Montreal Y.W.C.A. camp, located north of Montreal.' A native of Toronto, honours degree in Recreation from the University of Waterloo, several years full-time with the Saint John YWCA, Fellow of the Society of Camp Directors since 1977. She is only the SECOND named director of Oolahwan this project holds -- camp-oolahwan.md names nobody in charge between Mary Edgar's departure in 1919 and the final season in 2004 -- and her appointment shows Oolahwan was an operating YWCA residential camp in the late 1970s with a professional director recruited from another province. Search: YWCA Montreal records, YWCA Canada, the University of Waterloo Recreation alumni record, and Canadian Camping's own later issues, which the read will reach.
priorities.source: word-for-word read of Canadian Camping, issues 128-132, converted to KB facts

priorities.description: ASK CONCORDIA FOR A KANAWANA STAFF MANUAL BY NAME. Canadian Camping's Camp Staff Issue of February 1981 specifies exactly what one contained, in seven parts, and the specification is what makes this worth a targeted request rather than a general one. Part II, Facts About Camp: a directional map, 'a sketch of site showing trails, program areas, buildings', a description of the setting's special features and 'SPECIAL PROBLEMS WHICH SITE GIVES RISE TO'; statements of traditions and philosophy; 'a brief historical sketch of the camp'; and 'explanation of role that camping plays in the total program of the sponsoring organization' -- for Kanawana, the YMCA of Montreal. Personnel Policies: 'sickness allowance; employment and dismissal procedures; salary scales and payment procedures.' Part IV, the blank forms. Part V, job analyses for every post including the CIT programme. A single surviving Kanawana manual would carry all of that in one binder, and it would be the camp's own history as told to nineteen-year-olds, which is a franker document than a brochure. This also explains something the project already holds: the 'Kamp Kanawana History' presented at a staff training course in 1951 is precisely the 'brief historical sketch' the specification prescribes, so it was probably written for, or extracted from, a manual of this kind -- and others may exist for other years. Ask for staff manuals, counsellor manuals and camp manuals by all three names, and for the 1980 national training outline's Camp History session material.
priorities.source: word-for-word read of Canadian Camping, issues 133-137, converted to KB facts

priorities.description: SOURCE OR DROP THE CAMP KEEWAYDIN 1893 CLAIM. traditions/myths-and-legends.md has said since it was written that 'Camp Keewaydin in Ontario, founded in 1893, also predates Kanawana by one year.' The sentence cited f_0412, which says nothing about Keewaydin, and the KB holds no Keewaydin fact at all -- the citation was wrong and the claim is unsupported. It is now marked in the article as an unverified carry-over. Keewaydin's Canadian operation (Devil's Gap / Temagami) has a documented history and the date should be easy to establish or refute; Keewaydin Temagami is usually given as 1893 but the camp's origin is Vermont, 1893 or earlier, which may be what the original claim confused. Resolve it and either cite it properly or remove the sentence. Found while withdrawing the 'Canada's second-oldest' ranking after the Camp Stephens finding (c_031).
priorities.source: citation audit of myths-and-legends.md during the c_031 ranking withdrawal

priorities.description: TRIAGE THE CITATION-AIM BACK CATALOGUE AND MAKE THE CHECK BLOCKING. scripts/verify/citation_aim.py is advisory and currently reports two thin citations: (1) places-and-locations.md:223 cites f_0226 ('A 1928 Kanawana map and a 1962 Kanawana map were analyzed in the McMorris thesis') for the claim that an 'Indian Grave' marking existed on the camp map -- the fact establishes the maps but says nothing about the marking, so the specific claim is uncited; (2) myths-and-legends.md:108 cites f_0536 (a list of Cropsey name variants) for 'Both films derive from the same campfire tradition', which the fact does not state. Resolve both by finding the right fact or rewording the claim, then flip the script to exit 1 and move its workflow step above the embargo step. NOTE the check is a deliberately weak heuristic -- it compares distinctive tokens and passes any citation sharing one -- so a clean run is not proof of correct aim, only absence of the grossest shape. | COMPLETED 2026-09-05. citation_aim.py is now BLOCKING (exits 1) and its workflow step already sat above the embargo step. Four findings cleared, not two: the two in the queue plus two that surfaced behind them. (1) places-and-locations.md cited f_0226 ('a 1928 and a 1962 map were analyzed in the McMorris thesis') for the 'Indian Grave' marking; f_0228 states that claim exactly, same source, so the pointer was simply wrong and is corrected -- kb_facts_used updated with it. (2) myths-and-legends.md said 'Both films derive from the same campfire tradition [f_0536]', which f_0536 does not say; the sentence now states what the fact carries -- that Madman renamed its killer once The Burning was found to be using the Cropsey concept -- and an uncited Madman Marz backstory that appears in no KB fact went with it. Recorded in that article's Revision History. (3) and (4) oldest-camp-question.md:200 and :293 were both correctly aimed and tripped the heuristic because the distinctive name sat in the PREVIOUS sentence; both citing sentences now name Ottawa 1893 and Big Cove's four-summer gap respectively. That is the general remedy and it is printed in the failure message: a sentence carrying a citation should be checkable on its own. The check remains a weak heuristic -- one shared token passes it -- so a clean run is absence of the grossest shape, not proof of aim.

priorities.description: FOLD THE REMAINING ORPHANED MOVEMENT FIGURES INTO canadian-camping-movement.md -- DO NOT SPAWN STUBS FOR THEM. A coverage analysis on 2026-09-05 (facts.json entities vs. full-text search of every wiki article) found nine named individuals holding >=8 KB facts each whose names appear in NO wiki article at all: Margaret Govan (32 facts), Wallace Forgie (15), Elsie Palter (14), Keith Cleverdon (12), John Hoyle (11), Elizabeth Wardley Raymer (11), Doug Dent (11), David Palter (10), M. C. MacCulloch (8). Eleven more appear in exactly one article: Anne I. Vail (30), Joyce Bertram (28), Eileen Mayotte (15), Tony Shorgan (14), Paul Belanger (12), Janet Adamson (12), Sam Hambly (10), Dorothy Percival (9), Irwin Haladner (9), Gerard Bachand (9), Colette Pouliot-Marier (8). JUDGEMENT MADE AND RECORDED: these are Ontario and national camping-movement figures, not Kanawana people. Under the hub-and-spoke placement rules in CLAUDE.md, core people/ is for those who built and ran Kanawana, so none of these warrants its own article on present evidence and spawning nine to twenty stubs would bury the camp's own people. The right home is connections/institutional-lineage/canadian-camping-movement.md, plus the topic articles where a given figure is actually load-bearing. EXCEPTIONS worth revisiting if more turns up: Eileen Mayotte and Tony Shorgan are QUEBEC association figures with long runs (Mayotte QCA secretary in the 1940s through a national committee seat in 1987; Shorgan founded the French section in 1958 and was assembling the 1988 fiftieth-anniversary of Quebec camping, per p_319) -- either could earn a stub if a biography can be assembled. ALREADY ACTIONED: Govan's February 1958 'Stop Me If You've Heard This One' and McClelland's June 1956 'set a background whether true or fictitious' are written into traditions/myths-and-legends.md, because they date the deliberate manufacture of camp lore to within a decade of the year the Chopsy story claims for itself. | COUNTS REFRESHED 2026-09-05, AND THE METHOD BEHIND THEM QUALIFIED. Current state by exact-string search: Wallace Forgie 10 facts / 0 articles; Elsie Palter 14/0; John Hoyle 12/0; David Palter 14/0; Doug Dent 8/0; M. C. MacCulloch 7/0; Sam Hambly 6/0; Keith Cleverdon 4/0; Elizabeth Wardley Raymer 3/0. Margaret Govan has moved to 1 article (32 facts). TONY SHORGAN IS OFF THE LIST -- he now has his own article (p_336), which also means the 'appears in exactly one article' half of this priority is one name shorter. THE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS: this analysis matches exact strings, and people in this corpus appear under variant forms. 'Anne I. Vail' now scores 0 articles while the same woman appears throughout the wiki as NAN VAIL and ANN VAIL -- including in the Shorgan article written today. So both lists are approximations, the orphan list may name people who are in the wiki under another form, and any pass acting on this should search the variants before concluding a person is absent. The name_variants.py check in scripts/verify is the place that knowledge belongs. | DONE 2026-09-05, as instructed: FOLDED IN, NO STUBS SPAWNED. canadian-camping-movement.md gains a section, 'The people this article's sources keep naming', covering all nine -- Wallace Forgie (the 'Commodore', 1908-1927 in Canada, and Adele Ebbs's uncle, who took her on her first big canoe trip at ten); Elsie K. and David Palter of Camp Kawagama, on the editorial team of The Camp Counselor's Book, with Elsie Palter's own 1964 use of Maslow -- probably its earliest appearance in Canadian camping literature -- and her 1970 taxonomy of why children steal at camp; John Hoyle, who chaired the standards committee 1947-1950 and wrote the frankest ethics gloss in the run; Keith Cleverdon, who wrote that committee's documentary history in 1955; M. C. MacCulloch of Bolton Camp, whose 1969 discipline policy says 'In no instance may justice at camp take the form of physical punishment. We are not parents and these are not our children'; Elizabeth Wardley Raymer, whose 1958 account of a fouled canoe-trip site is a leave-no-trace argument twenty years early; Doug Dent of the 1974 Task Force; and Sam Hambly, whose composting pamphlet opened the association's HOW TO series. The section states why they are folded rather than spawned: none is documented as having any contact with Kanawana, and what they have is a claim on THIS article as the people whose written work the movement ran on. It also carries the name-variant caution, with Nan/Ann/Anne I. Vail as the worked example. All nine now appear in exactly one article, which is what the priority asked for.
priorities.source: coverage analysis of orphan facts after the Canadian Camping extraction pass

priorities.description: CLOSE THE ATTENDANCE-SERIES GAPS THAT THE '126 CONSECUTIVE SEASONS' CLAIM RESTS ON. canadian-camping-movement.md now states that Kanawana's longest unbroken run is 126 seasons (1894-2019), which beats Camp Stephens (~102) and Big Cove (~87) and is the one superlative that survives the continuity test. It depends on the camp having missed NO season in that span. No source records a missed season and the dangerous years are documented as operating (both wars, 1918 specifically, the 1946 polio outbreak), but meta/attendance-series.md has no figure at all for 1900, 1902-03, 1905-08, 1911, 1914, 1920, 1950-51, 1960-62, 1970-71, 1973, 1975-79, 1981-87, 1989-93, 1995, 1997, 2002-04 and 2006-19. Absence of a figure is not evidence of operation. Before the 126 is used publicly, establish operation (not attendance) for each missing year -- the annual reports carry a Kanawana line most years and the 1970s-80s season reports survive. ALSO OPEN: whether Camp Stephens ran in 2021 (explicit null, f_4747), and the 1917-vs-1918 date of its wartime closure (f_4744). | SUBSTANTIALLY ADVANCED 2026-09-05. Twenty-two seasons closed, and NOT ONE came from a new source: every document behind them was already in this repository, catalogued and marked extracted. The gap was an absence of assembly, not of evidence -- these files had been mined for programme, staff and buildings and their attendance lines never carried across. CLOSED WITH FIGURES: 1900 (45 boys, 28 June-14 July, six tents, eleven wet days of sixteen); 1903 (210, a figure this KB already held); 1907 (77 in two sections); 1962 (590 boys, 12,425 camper days); 1970 (1,442 camper weeks); 1971 (481 campers, 1,247 weeks, broken out by sex); 1973 (1,276); 1974 (1,264); 1975 (475 children, 1,356); 1976 (480, 1,358); 1977 (414, 1,174); 1978 (442, 1,227); 1979 (441 + 18 CITs, 1,375); 1985 (1,214, 80%); 1986 (1,400, 92.5%); 1987 (1,412, 93%). CLOSED AS OPERATING, NO FIGURE: 1902, 1905, 1908, 1950, 1951, 1960, 1961. ONE CORRECTION FORCED: the table's 475 at 1974 belongs to 1975 -- the 1975 director's report says so and gives 1974 as the lower year -- the fourth dated error in this wiki traceable to the June-May fiscal year. ONE COUNT ADDED: the 1975 director's report opens 'The eighty-second year of Kamp Kanawana has come to an end', a fifth institutional season-count consistent with an unbroken run from 1894 (f_4849). STILL BLANK: 1911, 1914, 1919, 1920, 1981-1984, 1989-1993, 1995-1997, 2002-04 and most of 2006-19. The 1990s are within reach through the plaque corpus, the Order of Owens roll and the L&V winners roll (which runs unbroken 1991-1998); the 2010s through the YMCAs of Quebec annual reports; 1911, 1914 and 1915 need annual-report volumes this project does not hold. The 126-season claim now rests partly on evidence and partly on silence, and both articles say so. | SECOND PASS SAME DAY, AND NOW CLOSED TO THREE YEARS. The reports run out before the record does. Two bodies of physical evidence already held here carry the seasons the reports skip. (1) THE PLAQUE CORPUS: the person index built from the boards (p_291) carries dated appearances for 1955, 1956, 1959-65, 1968, 1970, 1972, 1973, 1975, 1979-90 and 1992-2010. A board naming a cabin's campers and counsellor was made at camp in that summer, for those people -- direct physical evidence the season ran. Closes 1981-84, 1989-90, 1992-93, 1995-97, 2002-04 and 2006-2010 (f_4850). (2) THE L&V TROPHY: a shield for every season 1947-2025 but 2021, transcribed in full, closing every remaining year from 1976 forward -- WITH ITS OWN WARNING, since a 2020 shield exists and the camp did not run in 2020, the Games having been played remotely. A shield attests a season, not necessarily a residential one, and that is the one year in seventy-nine where the two come apart (f_4851). (3) 1906 came out of the same pass with a total of 216 across the Victoria Day party, Business Boys, School Boys and Seniors; the four components are illegible in the OCR and sit on the printed page for whoever reaches it (f_4852). STILL BLANK, AND NOW A QUESTION ABOUT THREE SPECIFIC BOOKS RATHER THAN A SCATTERED FORTY YEARS: 1911, 1914 and 1920, needing the annual reports published in 1912, 1915 and 1921, none of which is in the digitized run. Queued as p_420.
priorities.source: continuity research after the operator's question of 2026-09-05

priorities.description: READ 'LUMBERMEN & VOYAGEURS: THE YMCA PINE CREST STORY'. Camp Pine Crest's centennial history is the single most likely place for the origin of the Pine Crest Games (run every summer since 1940) and for any account of how the Lumbermen-and-Voyageurs competition reached Kanawana in 1947. Every public surface searched -- the YMCA of Greater Toronto's own blog on the Games, the camp pages, Wikipedia -- is silent on who created the Games, why the team names, and whether the tradition was passed to another camp. The book is sold through the camp's Shopify store. Buying or borrowing it is the action. Secondary: check whether Roy D. Locke, who became Kanawana's Camp Chief in the summer of 1947, had any prior Toronto or Pine Crest posting, and search Concordia P0145/12B for correspondence between the two camps in 1946-47.
priorities.source: expanded oldest-camp research and the inter-camp contact inquiry, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: TEST THE OTTAWA YMCA 1893 CLAIM AGAINST OTTAWA YMCA RECORDS. With Golden Lake 1884 resolved as an artefact of Sumner Dudley's American date, the surviving pre-Kanawana rival is Charles Plewman's statement that 'the Ottawa YMCA in 1893... began taking older boys to camp'. That is one year before Kanawana's first season and comes from a man who directed for the Ottawa Y himself. It has never been tested. Look for Ottawa YMCA annual reports of the 1890s, the 1893 board minute referenced in the Ace Milks profile, and any Camp On-Da-Da-Waks history. If 1893 holds, Kanawana is fourth rather than third among Canadian camps by founding date. | COMPLETED 2026-09-05. Tested on two surfaces and narrowed rather than closed. (1) The documentary half of the claim is an Ottawa YWCA board minute, not a YMCA record: Fraser's June 1954 profile says the origin of YMCA camping in Ottawa is 'somewhat lost in the mists of history' and that the first actual word of the camp that became On-Da-Da-Waks is a minute of an Ottawa Y.W.C.A. Board meeting recording a camp held in 1893 across from Quyon. Because OCR invents W/M, the page image was read directly (IA scan, leaf 12, cropped by the djvu word coordinates) and the printed text reads Y.W.C.A. f_2662 had it right; the wiki article was reading it as a YMCA record. New fact f_4835. (2) The Year Books of the YMCAs of North America 1893-1897, all five downloaded, cached in sources/cache/ymca-yearbooks/ and read (Ontario and Quebec reports in full, whole-volume search for 'camp' and 'tent'), record no camp for Ottawa -- and none for Montreal either, including the 1895 volume that reports on 1894. They report boys' camps elsewhere, so the silence is about coverage. That null cannot be used against Ottawa 1893 without also being used against Kanawana 1894. New fact f_4836, five new source records. (3) Byproduct: Charles Cushing was the International Committee's Corresponding Member for Quebec in 1893, 1894 and 1895 and signed the province's report in 1893 and 1895 -- name verified against the page image because the OCR reads GUSHING. New fact f_4837, written into cushing-family.md. f_4756 amended in place: not withdrawn, but its 'remains untested' tail is no longer true. What remains is offline and is now p_419.
priorities.source: expanded oldest-camp research and the inter-camp contact inquiry, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: ESTABLISH THE REAL NUMBER OF YMCA CAMPS IN CANADA, NOW AND OVER TIME. This project can date one solid figure -- twenty-nine YMCA camps took part in the 1989 centenary relay campfire, one hour each over twenty-nine hours -- and can name only six overnight YMCA camps in 2026 from separate association websites, because ymca.ca's national camps page names no individual camp. Stan Symington's 1953 tour of eastern Canada alone named nine, of which only Big Cove is identifiable as still operating. The apparent contraction is a comparison of three different instruments and must not be asserted until measured. YMCA Canada's national office would hold the series.
priorities.source: expanded oldest-camp research and the inter-camp contact inquiry, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: FOLD THE SIX COMPETING ORIGIN CLAIMS FOR CANADIAN CAMPING INTO ONE CONFLICT RECORD, as f_2845 recommended and as history/oldest-camp-question.md now needs. In play: Big Cove 1889/1890/1891; Camp Stephens 1891 vs Patton's 1894; Chance Harbour N.S. 1889; Ottawa YMCA 1893 (untested); Golden Lake 1884 (RESOLVED as an artefact, f_4754); Keewaydin 1893 (unsourced, p_400). They are currently scattered across c_029, c_031, individual facts and two articles.
priorities.source: expanded oldest-camp research and the inter-camp contact inquiry, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: READ KNOW HISTORY'S 'ROOTED: BEAUSOLEIL ISLAND', CHAPTER 5: CAMP KITCHIKEWANA -- AND REOPEN THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL OF THE L&V GAMES. The operator surfaced on 2026-09-05 that YMCA Camp Kitchikewana runs 'Lumberman and Voyageur Games', a third Canadian YMCA camp with the tradition after Pine Crest (from 1940) and Kanawana (from 1947). Kitchikewana was founded in 1919, twenty-one years before the Pine Crest Games, so the working assumption that Pine Crest originated the competition and Kanawana borrowed it is now untested -- the tradition may have moved the other way, or all three may draw on a common source. Neither Kitchikewana page dates its Games. Know History's commissioned study of Beausoleil Island has a chapter on the camp and returns HTTP 403 to this project's fetch tool; try a browser, a library copy, or Parks Canada, which commissioned work on the island. Pair with p_404 (the Pine Crest centennial history). ALSO: Kitchikewana's founding is disputed in this project's own records -- 1919 per the camp and the KB, 1921 per C. R. Blackstock's obituary and the Ebbs tribute, both describing him as an 'original' who started in the camp's first year. | COMPLETED 2026-09-05, with the premise corrected. 'Rooted: Beausoleil Island' IS NOT A STUDY. It is an eight-chapter audio podcast published 18 October 2021 -- there was never anything to read, which is why the URL held here 404s to a browser user-agent while the site returns 200. The 403 recorded earlier was a true fact about the fetch tool and a misleading one about the object. Chapter 5 (12m10s) was downloaded and transcribed by machine in-session, since no transcript is published, and read in full: archaeology of the camp's sandy point, the Parks Canada partnership, and Brian Shelley on what the place did for him. NOTHING ABOUT THE L&V GAMES -- lumberman, voyageur, games, competition, team, colour war, Kanawana and Pine Crest are all absent from the 1,412-word transcript (f_4841); the caveat that a machine transcript is the audio filtered through a model travels with the null. It does state 1919 twice ('In 2019, Camp Kitchikewana celebrated its 100th anniversary'), a third voice for that date but not an independent one, since the camp took part in the programme -- the 1919-vs-1921 conflict stands (f_4842). points-of-contact.md updated, 26 -> 27 sources; the transcript is cached with a header stating what it is. THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL REMAINS OPEN and p_404, the Pine Crest centennial history, is now the only identified published route to it.
priorities.source: operator surfaced the Kitchikewana L&V Games, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: SURVEY CANADIAN CAMPS FOR THE LUMBERMEN-AND-VOYAGEURS COMPETITION -- THE COUNT IS A FLOOR AND THIS PROJECT'S SEARCHES ARE NOT FINDING THEM. Four camps are now documented: Camp Pine Crest (Games from 1940), Kanawana (1947), Camp Kitchikewana (undated) and RKY Camp (undated). BOTH additions beyond the original two came from the operator recognising a camp, not from any search this project ran, which is itself the finding: the tradition is more widespread than these searches surface. Method: query the Ontario Camps Association member list camp by camp for 'Lumbermen', 'Voyageurs', 'the Games'; check YMCA associations across Ontario and Quebec; check camps with YMCA roots now independently owned, as RKY is. Establish for each the date the tradition began. The prize is the direction of travel: Kitchikewana (founded 1919) and RKY (1930) both predate the Pine Crest Games of 1940, so the assumption that Pine Crest originated it and Kanawana borrowed it is untested, and only Kanawana's 1947 adoption carries a date at all. [PARTIAL 2026-09-05. INSTRUMENT FOUND: the OCA member directory, 163 camps, paginated by ?alpha=N, with 61 YMCA/YWCA entries on its Y page -- the systematic tool the earlier searches lacked. CHECKED: Camp Queen Elizabeth (negative), Camp Waabanaki (negative -- its Voyageurs is an extended tripping programme, confirming the Big Cove rank-versus-team distinction), Big Cove (negative). STILL FOUR confirmed: Pine Crest, Kanawana, Kitchikewana, RKY. UNCHECKED: a dozen-plus Ontario YMCA overnight camps -- Wanakita, Belwood, Ki-Wa-Y, Heidelberg, Tillicum, John Island, Camp Henry, Otonabee, Geneva Park, Cedar Glen, Rotary Youth Camp Presqu'ile -- plus every non-YMCA OCA member and the whole ACQ membership in Quebec. METHOD NOTE: phrase search does not work; camp programme pages do not rank. Enumerate the directory camp by camp. Also correct: this project's count of YMCA overnight camps in Canada was badly low and has been relabelled in the article as a list of camps discussed, not a census.] [COMPLETE 2026-09-05 for Ontario's YMCA overnight camps: ten checked, ten negative -- Belwood, Ki-Wa-Y, Waabanaki, Wanakita, Camp Henry, Camp Queen Elizabeth, Tillicum, John Island, Otonabee, Presqu'ile. Count stands at four. KEY RESULT: the colour-war GENRE is common (John Island runs 'Colour Wars', Presqu'ile runs 'Presqu'ile Bound') but the Lumbermen-and-Voyageurs NAMING is confined to four camps, making it a minority practice within its own movement and implying a specific rather than systemic route -- look for a PERSON who moved between Pine Crest, Kitchikewana, RKY and Kanawana. STILL OPEN and now handed to p_404 and p_408: no camp dates its Games beyond Pine Crest 1940 and Kanawana 1947. NOT DONE: non-YMCA OCA members and the entire ACQ membership in Quebec, either of which could hold a fifth camp.]
priorities.source: operator surfaced Kitchikewana and RKY on 2026-09-05; two searches had missed both

priorities.description: FIX THE START DATE OF KANAWANA'S L&V GAMES FROM A CONTEMPORARY DOCUMENT. This wiki asserts 1947, sourced to the YMCA's modern count of a 78th edition in 2025. That arithmetic does not yield 1947: run without gaps it gives 1948, and excluding the two COVID years it gives 1946. The earliest contemporary mention in this project's cache is the 1950 annual report, which already calls the tradition established and says the two-team week 'again' met with enthusiasm. The annual reports for 1947, 1948 and 1949 are silent on it, and the camp's own 1951 history never mentions it while listing Locke's other innovations. WHERE TO LOOK: Concordia P0145/12B, the Kanawana season and director's reports for 1946-1949; the Green Triangle and other camp newsletters of those years; and the YMCA's own basis for the edition count. Until then the 1947 date should be described as approximate wherever it appears -- traditions/lv-games.md, the timeline, and points-of-contact.md.
priorities.source: chasing the Locke transmission hypothesis, 2026-09-05
priorities.resolution: WITHDRAWN AS MISCONCEIVED, AND THE DATE CONFIRMED. This priority's premise was wrong on both halves and both were checkable against material already in the KB when it was written. (1) The wiki did not source 1947 only to the modern edition count: 'Kanawana... A Place to Grow' (1988) states the 1947 creation outright under Programme Highlights, and the perpetual Annual Trophy's first shield reads 47 -- both already extracted (f_1996, f_2000) and both already cited in traditions/lv-games.md. (2) The arithmetic does yield 1947: it failed only because it deducted TWO pandemic seasons where the record carries one. 2020 was contested remotely and has a shield; only 2021 is missing. 1947-2025 is 79 seasons, less 2021 is 78 -- YMCA Quebec's 78th edition for 2025, exactly. See f_4798; f_4796 superseded. What remains open is narrower and has been rewritten into points-of-contact.md Open Question 2: no CONTEMPORARY document from 1947-1949 mentions the tradition, so the founding seasons are attested only retrospectively. Concordia P0145/12B would close that; it does not put the year in doubt.

priorities.description: FIX scripts/verify/seed_read_state.py -- IT CLOBBERS PROVENANCE. Run on 2026-09-05 (by accident, in a loop over scripts/verify/*.py) it reported 'updated: 14' and rewrote read_state_basis on fourteen Kanawana report records from 'derived:cited-by-fact | cached text linked 2026-09-02: the file was on disk under no record' down to the bare 'derived:cited-by-fact'. The hand-added clause -- the note that the cached text was found orphaned on disk and linked back to a record -- is exactly the kind of thing this project keeps and exactly what the no-silent-overwrite rule protects. The script recomputes the field from scratch and writes unconditionally instead of merging, so any manual annotation is destroyed on every run, and it reserialises the whole file (28k lines) so the damage is invisible in a diff. The change was reverted before it reached main. FIX: make the script append or merge rather than replace, leave a hand-written basis alone, preserve the existing serialisation, and print what it would change under a --dry-run before it writes anything. It is not a CI step, so nothing caught this but reading the diff.
priorities.source: caught reviewing the p_410 correction commit, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: 93 OF 100 'disputed' FACTS CARRY NO CONFLICT RECORD. CLAUDE.md's conflict rule says that when a new fact contradicts an existing one the response is to create a conflict record linking both and flag it for review. In practice most contradictions were recorded only as fact-to-fact conflicts_with links, or as confidence:disputed with nothing linked at all. The consequence is that kb/conflicts.json -- the file 'kb-conflicts' reads, and the file a human scans to see what still needs deciding -- undercounts the real number of live disagreements by roughly an order of magnitude. Sixteen of the 93 have no conflicts_with entry of any kind, so nothing anywhere records what they are disputed AGAINST; those are the worst, because a later reader cannot reconstruct the disagreement. TASK: triage the 93. For each, either (a) raise a conflict record, (b) resolve it if the KB already answers it, or (c) downgrade the confidence if 'disputed' was never right. Do NOT bulk-generate 93 conflict records -- several will turn out to be the same disagreement seen from both sides, and a pair should produce one record, not two. Surfaced by scripts/verify/staleness.py, which reports the count on every run. | THE TAIL CLOSED 2026-09-05. The four disputed facts that still carried no c_ conflict record are done, and three of them turned out to be a category slip rather than an oversight. f_4840 (Camp Stephens's 1911 boys' camp) simply lacked the link and now carries c_063. The other three were labelled 'disputed' for facts whose own content is not contested: f_2229 is a true statement that two outside sources disagree about Terry Mosher's Order of Canada year, with an earlier pass's reasoned decision not to open conflict records because neither touches a Kanawana claim -- that decision stands; f_1882 records a debunking this project withdrew and then saw confirmed in print; f_4808 records a correction made within the hour of the fact being written. All three are now 'stated', each with a note saying what was reclassified and why. THE GENERAL POINT, worth keeping: using 'disputed' both for a contested claim and for a fact that REPORTS a disagreement makes the disputed count mean two things at once, and this project reads that count as a work queue. staleness.py now reports 0 of 59.
priorities.source: whole-build staleness sweep, 2026-09-05
priorities.resolution: DONE. All 93 read in full and triaged; decisions recorded per fact in kb/triage/p412_disputed_triage.json. 29 linked to conflicts that already existed; 24 new conflict records raised (c_039-c_062) covering 32 facts, grouped so that one disagreement seen from two sides produces one record; 32 downgraded because 'disputed' was never right for them -- 21 to stated (nulls, access failures, exhausted searches, one debunking) and 9 to inferred (single low-reliability sources and unproven identifications) and 2 superseded facts set to stated behind their markers. One kept disputed on purpose: f_2229, whose own text records the decision not to escalate discrepancies that touch no Kanawana claim. Disputed 100 -> 60; without a conflict record 93 -> 1; conflicts 38 -> 62. SECOND PASS: the linking itself surfaced ten facts still disputed under already-resolved conflicts, invisible until the link existed; each adjudicated by reading which side of the resolution it fell on. Also normalised five conflicts whose resolution text sat in the notes field, where a reader checking `resolution` would have seen a blank and concluded nothing was decided.

priorities.description: ONE PIP RECIPIENT STILL UNACCOUNTED FOR, plus three sets of camp years. The 2026 release (src_ymca_quebec_pip_macsween_2026) fixed the ordinals -- Orbinski 15th/2024, MacSween 17th/2026, so the 16th is 2025 -- and named two recipients this project had never heard of: Dr. Karl Cernovich (2020-2023 on the release's chronological ordering) and Alexandra Olshefsky (2025). Fourteen preceded Orbinski; this wiki can now name thirteen; ONE remains, either a 2010 recipient or a second award in 2020-2023 (f_4809). ASK THE COMMITTEE FOR ITS OWN LIST -- the method question is settled: roughly sixty queries failed on 2019 and it closed in a sentence by asking, and two further recipients were simply unknown until the sponsor's release was handed over. While asking, get: Cernovich's year; the Kanawana years for Ornstein, Cernovich and Olshefsky, none of which any source gives; and whether 2010 had an award at all.

priorities.description: THREE NEW NAMED PEOPLE FROM THE 2026 PIP RELEASE, none previously in this project: JARED MACSWEEN (2026 recipient; Kanawana camper 1982-86 and staff 1987-91; GM of YMCA Cedar Glen Outdoor Centre; Manager of Training at the YMCA Ontario Regional Development Centre 2012-24; BA Applied Human Science and Diploma in Social Studies, Concordia), DR. KARL CERNOVICH (emergency medicine) and ALEXANDRA OLSHEFSKY (public defender). MacSween already clears this project's article-spawning threshold on the biography alone -- a named person who held a camp role, with dated camper and staff years and a documented career -- and his YMCA Ontario posting is directly relevant to the L&V transmission question, since Cedar Glen and the Ontario RDC sit inside the same association network as Pine Crest and Kitchikewana. ASSESS whether to spawn stubs; if so they go in people/ (core), not people/notable-alumni/, since the defining connection for MacSween is a career inside the YMCA rather than a life lived outside it. REVISED 2026-09-05: OLSHEFSKY IS NO LONGER A ONE-LINE ENTRY and was never new to this project -- she is on the Rangers 2002 plaque and the Knights of Kanawana roll (f_4815), was a camper through 2002 per the operator who was staff that year (f_4816), and is the only person documented holding both a knighthood and the Pip Award (f_4818). That is enough for a stub. DR. KARL CERNOVICH genuinely is new and has one line; he should wait for a year and a camp connection. Ask the operator, who plainly knows this cohort, for Olshefsky's staff years if any, and for Cernovich's year. | PARTIALLY COMPLETE 2026-09-05. JARED MACSWEEN: article spawned at wiki/people/jared-macsween.md, and deliberately as a STUB rather than a draft -- the pipeline's draft bar is three sources and this has one carrying source (the 2026 release) plus one negative (he is absent from the plaque person index, which covers 1979-1990; a fact about which boards survived, not about whether he was there). A web search on 2026-09-05 for his name against the YMCA Cedar Glen Outdoor Centre returned nothing beyond the release -- no staff page, no news item, no directory entry -- and that null is recorded in the article so a later pass does not repeat it. PLACED IN CORE people/, not notable-alumni/, on CLAUDE.md's own folder test: nine seasons at camp (camper 1982-86, staff 1987-91) are the reason he is here, and he would carry no Wikipedia-notable article without Kanawana. Indexed into directors-index.md's alumni table -- which was four recipients out of date, so Ornstein (2019), Cernovich (2020-23), Olshefsky (2025) and MacSween (2026) were all added -- and linked from pip-alumni-award.md. Four open questions, the sharpest being whether his Concordia Applied Human Science degree runs through the department Hedley Dimock built out of YMCA work with Kanawana as its field site. STILL OPEN: ALEXANDRA OLSHEFSKY, whose staff years remain unknown -- the wiki has 'former staff' from the release and camper/Ranger/Knight standing in 2002 from two plaques. That is a question for Matt, not a search. KARL CERNOVICH does not clear the threshold and no article is spawned.
priorities.source: 2026 Pip Award release supplied by the operator, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: RECOVER CAROL SKINNER'S BLOG FROM THE INTERNET ARCHIVE. 'Live Love Laugh with Carol' (livelovelaughwithcarol.com) was her own long-form account of living with ALS, named by ALS Canada in its 2021 memorial as 'a source of positivity and strength for many'. IT IS THE ONLY FIRST-PERSON, LONG-FORM SOURCE THIS PROJECT HAS EVER IDENTIFIED FOR ANY KANAWANA PERSON WRITING ABOUT THEIR OWN LIFE. The domain has since been taken over and now serves an Indonesian online-gambling site (f_4825), so a reader who checks the address today would reasonably conclude the blog never existed. web.archive.org is blocked by THIS ENVIRONMENT'S egress policy, not by the archive -- ANYONE WITH AN ORDINARY BROWSER CAN DO THIS IN MINUTES. Known section structure from search indexes: Love Story, ALS, Blog, Tips & Tricks, Gallery, Travel, Media. Look for: her Kanawana years in her own words, the section(s) she directed 1990-95, her Camp Hayward years, and anything on the camp's influence on her later work. HIGH VALUE, LOW EFFORT, AND DEGRADING -- archived captures are not guaranteed to persist.

priorities.description: MAKE articles.json's DERIVED COUNTS SELF-MAINTAINING, OR STOP CARRYING THEM. On 2026-09-05 a recompute found 54 OF 104 RECORDS -- better than half -- carrying a stale word_count or open_questions. Two causes. (1) Nothing recomputes them: they are written by hand whenever an article is edited, so they drift from the moment they are set, and a reader has no way to tell a current figure from a year-old one. (2) Six articles numbered their Open Questions list from 0 rather than 1, so every count taken off those lists was short by one; all six are now renumbered. The word_count field also uses Python str.split() semantics, which do not match `wc -w` -- a difference that misled this project's own operator report today until it was checked directly. FIX: either add a builder like scripts/plaque/build_index.py and have data_integrity.py assert the file matches it -- the pattern this repo already uses for the multi-year index and which works -- or drop both fields, since a stale number is worse than no number. Prefer the builder: word_count and open_questions are genuinely useful for triage, and p_412 showed how quickly an unmaintained field stops being read at all. | COMPLETED 2026-09-05. Builder route taken, not the drop-the-fields route. scripts/wiki/build_article_counts.py now generates word_count, open_questions and article_count, and data_integrity.py regenerates wiki/articles.json into a scratch copy and fails if the committed file differs -- the arrangement the plaque index already uses. Fifty of 104 records carried a stale open_questions and article_count read 93 against 104 records, eleven articles behind. word_count was already current (all 104 matched), so the definition it was computed under is the one the builder keeps, documented in the module docstring including why it is not `wc -w`. open_questions is now the count of entries that are still OPEN: an entry struck through, or opening with an unqualified [Resolved]/[ANSWERED] tag, is not counted, while [Partially resolved] and [Largely resolved] are, because a remainder is a remainder. That is why most counts fell -- 103 of 470 listed questions are answered in place. STILL OPEN, deliberately: three articles number their Open Questions lists 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,7,8 (coeducation-gender), 1..7,9,10,8 (myths-and-legends) and 1..7,7,8,9 (camp-songs-cheers). The builder reports them and does not renumber, because other articles cite questions by number ('billy-ball Open Question #8') and shifting a number silently re-points a citation at a different question. Renumbering needs a pass over the citing articles at the same time.
priorities.source: checking the matt-aronson record, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: SETTLE WHETHER KANAWANA'S KATIMAVIK IS NAMED FOR THE FEDERAL KATIMAVIK PROGRAMME, and read the 1977-79 record around the opening. Three things sit together in 1978 and nothing connects them (f_4833): the camp opened a recreation hall called Katimavik; staff member John Lawrence was living inside the federal Katimavik programme, created 1977, per Ka-News October and December 1978 (f_4832); and Pierre Elliott Trudeau, whose government created that programme, sent the camp a congratulatory letter (f_4828). A camp naming a building in Inuktitut in the 1970s needs no federal explanation, so this must not be written up as a connection on the coincidence alone. WHERE TO LOOK: the full Ka-News run for 1977-79 (several issues are already cached and were read only for other purposes), the 1977 and 1979 director's reports, and the $850,000 reconstruction file behind f_2443 -- a building that size will have a naming decision somewhere. ALSO WORTH ASKING ANYONE WHO WAS THERE. SECOND QUESTION, SAME SOURCES: what stood on the Katimavik site before 1978, which places-and-locations.md Open Question 3 still carries. THIRD: whether other framed correspondence hangs at camp -- this letter was unknown to the project until the operator photographed it, and a Prime Minister's letter is unlikely to be the only thing on those walls.
priorities.source: operator-supplied photograph of the framed Trudeau letter, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: THE TWO OFFLINE ROUTES TO OTTAWA 1893, THE ONLY ONES LEFT. p_405 tested the claim on every surface reachable from here and narrowed it: what is left is one man's recollection (Plewman, December 1964) plus a minute of an Ottawa YWCA board meeting, quoted second-hand in 1954, about a camp whose sponsor is not stated (f_4835). Neither has been seen. TWO DOCUMENTS WOULD SETTLE IT. (1) The Ottawa YMCA's own annual reports of the 1890s -- not digitized anywhere this project can reach; the YMCA-YWCA of the National Capital Region and the City of Ottawa Archives (which holds Ottawa Y material) are the places to ask. (2) The Ottawa YWCA minute book Arnold Fraser was reading in 1954, which is the actual paper behind the 1893 date. NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE QUESTION: if the 1893 camp was a YWCA camp, it is not a rival to Kanawana at all on the YMCA-camp comparison, and Plewman's sentence stands alone. If it was a joint or YMCA camp that the YWCA board happened to minute, Ottawa is one year ahead. Do not record either reading without the document. NEEDS A HUMAN or a written enquiry -- this is an archive request, not a search.
priorities.source: p_405 test of the Ottawa YMCA 1893 claim, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: THREE ANNUAL REPORTS, THREE SEASONS: 1911, 1914 AND 1920. After both fills of 2026-09-05 the attendance series has exactly three seasons with no evidence of operation at all, and each needs one specific volume: the YMCA of Montreal annual reports covering those seasons, published in 1912, 1915 and 1921. NONE IS IN THE DIGITIZED RUN -- it jumps 1910 to 1913, the 1915 volume carries no Kanawana content, and it jumps 1920 to 1921-1922. WHY IT MATTERS: the 126-consecutive-seasons claim (1894-2019) is the one superlative that survives the continuity test, and these three are the only years left where it rests on silence. WHERE TO LOOK: Concordia Archives holds the YMCA of Montreal fonds and the full report series in print (add to the p_282 letter); Internet Archive may hold volumes catalogued under a title this project has not searched; BAnQ and the McGill and McCord collections hold Montreal association material. ALSO WORTH ONE PASS: the Montreal Gazette for July and August of 1911, 1914 and 1920 -- the paper covered the camp in 1918 and would likely have noticed a season that did not happen.
priorities.source: p_403 second fill, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: ASK THE TAYLOR STATTEN CAMPS WHETHER EASTAUGH'S CEREMONY DOCUMENT SURVIVES. Writing in Canadian Camping in Spring 1973, Jack Eastaugh, Assistant to the Director of the Taylor Statten Camps, offered readers 'a complete and detailed description of the rituals, ceremonies, games and organization' of the Indian Council Ring on request. THAT IS THE VERSION KANAWANA'S LEADERS WERE TAUGHT. p_368 has now established that the printed ancestor is Seton's Book of Woodcraft of 1912 and traced the closing chant to Alice Fletcher's Omaha fieldwork, but between Seton's book and a Laurentian camp's script stands Taylor Statten's teaching of the 1920s, and Eastaugh's document is the closest surviving form of it. ASK: the Taylor Statten Camps (Camps Ahmek and Wapomeo, Canoe Lake, Algonquin Park) directly; the Ontario Camping Association fonds at Trent University Archives, which holds the association's own papers and taped interviews (p_348); and the Ahmek/Statten family papers if they are deposited anywhere. NEEDS A HUMAN or a written enquiry.
priorities.source: p_368 Seton comparison, 2026-09-05

queue_ordering.scheme: Three tiers per operator direction 2026-08-25. (1) YIELD -- what returns the most new information per unit of effort: whole seams, not single facts. (2) INGESTION -- reaching and extracting material already within reach. (3) RALPH -- verify, refine and draft articles from what has been ingested. Within a tier: hand-ordered where the ordering was reasoned, then assigned_weight. Ten Concordia asks were folded into p_282 rather than left as separate lines.
